newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen extending gains Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares rose in higher trade and analysts saw further growth on Thursday after most stocks rose in the continuous trade, but expected the bourse to remain locked in its 13-week sideways drift in longer-term.

The main market's WIG index rose 125.6 points, or 0.8 percent, to 16,119.3 on Wednesday, and turnover rose 16 percent to 120.6 million zlotys ($37.7 million) on all three markets as 50 issues rose, 25 fell and 30 were flat.

"I think we still have the same situation on the market, still low turnovers...we can have growth tomorrow, but there are no indications that the market would establish a clear trend in either direction," said Tomasz Berent of IB Austria.
Analysts said Thursday's session would be dominated by 15 National Investment Funds' debut, which might bring some fresh air to the rather drowsy market.

Analysts said the upside, where some stocks already seemed undervalued, was limited by Bank Handlowy current public offering worth one billion zlotys ($312 million) and copper concern KGHM offering due to begin on June 30, worth at least 300 million zlotys ($93 million).
They said fortcoming elections due in September were additionally cooling investor demand.

Bank Rozwoju Eksportu surged 9.9 percent on news that Germany's Commerzbank AG might increase its stake in the bank to over 50 percent and analysts said it was likely to extend gains in the next few sessions.
Warta insurer rose 9.1 percent in a moderate turnover, rebounding after its unexpected fall 10 percent on Tuesday.
In the continuous trade 12 stocks rose, one fell and five were flat with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,649.6 points, 1.7 percent higher that at the regular session.
